title: Cap. IX: Garissoles (4) — whole-sentence softener; Placeus answers, does not assert
pass_a_gloss: Fourth, Garissoles grants that the phrase may soften the whole sentence 'Levi was tithed in Abraham,' then asks what that helps the adversary. Tithe-payment was Abraham's own personal act alone; attributing it also to the Levites admits speech-impropriety — not proper and personal, but interpretive and by imputation, as if they are reckoned to have done what Abraham alone did. What others did and is imputed to us is not 'ours' the way our own deeds are, per the Poet: what we ourselves did not do I scarcely call ours. Placeus: Garissoles has forgotten his role. He answers where he should prove. Placeus does not affirm those apostolic words as his own thesis; he only meets the objections and shows they do not hurt his cause — enough for him. Garissoles meanwhile grants the needed point: there is speech-impropriety that wants softening. So Garissoles had to prove that impropriety still lets opponents press the verse against Placeus. He never does.
pass_b_english: Fourth: "Granted," he says, "that that phrase also belongs to softening the whole sentence — 'Levi was tithed in Abraham' — what help is that to the adversary's cause? For the payment of tithes was certainly Abraham's own personal act alone. Therefore when it is attributed to the Levites as well, a certain impropriety of speech must be owned: it is attributed to them not properly and personally, but interpretatively and by imputation, insofar as they are reckoned to have done what Abraham alone had done. For what others have performed, and what is imputed to us, is not called properly ours in the same way as what we ourselves did — according to that of the Poet: 'And what we ourselves did not do, I scarcely call ours.'" First, though, he seems to have forgotten what part he ought to play. For he answers when he ought to prove. We certainly do not assert those words of the Apostle; we only answer what has been brought forward and objected, and we make plain that it in no way harms our cause — and that is enough for us. Meanwhile he grants what we want: that there is a certain impropriety of speech that needs softening. It was therefore his to show and prove that such impropriety does not keep the words of that place from being pressed so as to serve those who attack us. But this he does not do at all.
source_text: 4. Esto, inquit, etiam phrasim illam ad molliendam totam sententiam pertinere, Levi decimatus est in Abrahamo, quid hoc juvat causam adversariam? Certe enim decimarum persolutio fuit actio propria & personalis solius Abrahami. Ergo cum ea Levitis etiam tribuitur, est agnoscenda quaedam sermonis improprietas; non enim proprie & personaliter, sed interpretative & per imputationem eis tribuitur, quatenus illi reputantur fecisse id quod Abrahamus solus fecerat; Neque enim quae praestita sunt ab aliis & nobis imputantur, ita proprie nostra dicuntur, sicut ea quae ipsi fecimus, juxta illud Poetae, Et quae non fecimus ipsi, vix ea nostra voco. Primum autem oblitus videtur quas agere partes debeat. Respondet enim, cum probare debeat. Nos certe verba illa Apostoli non asserimus; allatis & objectis respondemus duntaxat, ac palam facimus ei causae nostrae nullo modo obesse: id quod nobis satis est. Interim concedit quod volumus, esse sermonis improprietatem quandam egentem emollitione. Ejus igitur erat ostendere & probare hujusmodi improprietatem non impedire, quominus illius loci verba sic urgeantur, ut ab iis sit qui nos oppugnant. Hoc vero minime facit.

choices.decision: Garissoles must prove urge despite impropriety; Placeus only answers
